facts.text: India became independent in 1947 CE.
facts.quote: India became independent in 1947 ce.

facts.text: India accepted the constitutional framework in 1950 and became a sovereign democratic nation.
facts.quote: India accepted the constitutional framework in 1950 and became a sovereign democratic nation.

facts.text: Indian society is multicultural: people of various languages, religions, ethnicities and castes live together.
facts.quote: The Indian society is multicultural and people of various languages, religions, ethnicities and castes live together.

facts.text: The establishment of the Planning Commission and emphasis on industrialisation were a means to achieve economic development and eliminate poverty.
facts.quote: The establishment of the Planning Commission and emphasis on industrialisation was a means to achieve economic development and to eliminate poverty in India.

facts.text: In the 1960s the regions of Goa, Diu and Daman were freed from Portuguese rule and became parts of the Indian federation.
facts.quote: The regions of Goa, Diu and Daman were freed from Portuguese rule and became parts of the Indian federation.

facts.text: Tensions between India and China on the northern border, rising since 1950, culminated in the war of 1962, fought in the region of the MacMahon line.
facts.quote: The tensions between India and China on the northern border which had been rising since 1950, culminated in the war of 1962 between two countries. This war was fought in the region of the MacMahon line.

facts.text: Prime Minister Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru led the country after independence; he was the architect of India's foreign policy.
facts.quote: After India became independent, Prime Minister Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru led the country. He was the architect of India's foreign policy.

facts.text: Jawaharlal Nehru passed away in 1964; Lal Bahadur Shastri succeeded him as Prime Minister.
facts.quote: Jawaharlal Nehru passed away in 1964. Lal Bahadur Shastri succeeded him and became the next Prime Minister of India.

facts.text: During Shastri's tenure India and Pakistan went to war over the Kashmir issue in 1965; the Soviet Russia tried to mediate.
facts.quote: During his tenure, India and Pakistan went to war over the Kashmir issue in 1965. The Soviet Russia tried to mediate between the two countries.

facts.text: Lal Bahadur Shastri breathed his last at Tashkent in 1966.
facts.quote: Lal Bahadur Shastri breathed his last at Tashkent in 1966.

facts.text: Lal Bahadur Shastri gave the slogan 'Jai Jawan Jai Kisan', highlighting Indian soldiers and Indian farmers.
facts.quote: Lal Bahadur Shastri gave the slogan 'Jai Jawan Jai Kisan' with which he highlighted the importance of Indian soldiers and Indian farmers.

facts.text: Indira Gandhi became Prime Minister in 1966; her decisions on nationalisation of banks and cancelling pensions of Princes had far reaching effects.
facts.quote: Indira Gandhi became the Prime Minister of India in 1966. ... Her decisions regarding the Nationalisation of banks and cancelling pensions of Princes had far reaching effects.

facts.text: Pakistan's oppressive policies in East Pakistan led to a big movement led by Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and his organisation 'Mukti Bahini'; millions of refugees came to India.
facts.quote: Pakistan's oppressive policies in East Pakistan resulted in a big movement there. This movement was led by Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and his organisation, 'Mukti Bahini.' This crisis in East Pakistan affected India as well, because millions of refugees came to India.

facts.text: The 1971 war between India and Pakistan led to the creation of an independent country called Bangladesh; Indira Gandhi's strong leadership was prominent.
facts.quote: The 1971 war between India and Pakistan led to the creation of an independent country called Bangladesh. Role of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's strong leadership was prominent in this issue.

facts.text: As part of the policy to use atomic energy for peaceful purposes, India carried out an underground test of an atomic device at Pokharan in Rajasthan in 1974.
facts.quote: As a part of India's policy to use atomic energy for peaceful purposes, India successfully carried out an underground test of an atomic device at Pokharan in Rajasthan in 1974.

facts.text: In 1975 the people of Sikkim voted for joining the Indian republic and Sikkim became a full-fledged State.
facts.quote: In 1975, the people of Sikkim voted for joining the Indian republic and Sikkim became a full-fledged State in the Indian federation.

facts.text: During the National Emergency (1975 to 1977) fundamental rights were suspended; administration became disciplined but human rights were restricted; general elections followed.
facts.quote: During this turbulent period, the fundamental rights of Indian citizens were suspended. Due to the emergency, the Indian administration became disciplined, but the human rights were restricted. The period of national emergency lasted from 1975 to 1977 and after that general elections were conducted.

facts.text: Opposition parties formed the Janata Party, which roundly defeated the Congress; Morarji Desai became Prime Minister but the government could not last long due to internal differences; Charan Singh succeeded him, also short-lived.
facts.quote: many opposition parties came together and formed a party called the Janata Party. The Congress party led by Indira Gandhi was roundly defeated ... Morarji Desai became the Prime Minister, but ... the Janata Party government couldn't last long due to internal differences. Charan Singh succeeded him, but even his government was a short-lived one.

facts.text: Elections were held again in 1980 and the Congress under Indira Gandhi came to power again.
facts.quote: Elections were conducted once again in 1980 and the Congress party under the leadership of Indira Gandhi came to power again.

facts.text: In the 1980s Sikhs in Punjab demanded an independent state of Khalistan; the movement became violent and destructive, and Pakistan lent its support.
facts.quote: The Sikhs in Punjab demanded an independent state of Khalistan and began a movement which went on to become violent and destructive. Pakistan had lent its support to this movement.

facts.text: In 1984 the Indian army was sent into the Golden Temple at Amritsar, a holy shrine of the Sikhs, to evict terrorists; a bodyguard in Indira Gandhi's personal security assassinated her.
facts.quote: The Indian army was sent into the Golden Temple at Amritsar, a holy shrine of the Sikhs in 1984, to evict the terrorists who had allegedly taken shelter there. One of the bodyguards in Indira Gandhi's personal security assassinated her.

facts.text: The United Liberation Front of Assam (ULFA) carried on a major movement in North-east India.
facts.quote: During this period, an organisation called United Liberation Front of Assam (ULFA) carried on a major movement in North-east India.

facts.text: Right after Indira Gandhi's assassination in 1984, Rajiv Gandhi became Prime Minister; he tried reforms in the economy and in science and technology.
facts.quote: Right after Indira Gandhi's assassination in 1984, Rajiv Gandhi became the Prime Minister of India. He tried to make several reforms in the field of Indian economy and that of science and technology.

facts.text: Rajiv Gandhi took the lead in solving the issues of the Tamil minority in Sri Lanka, promoting a united Sri Lanka with internal autonomy to the Tamil community, but in vain.
facts.quote: He took the lead in solving the issues of the Tamil minority in Sri Lanka. He promoted the idea of a united Sri Lanka with internal autonomy to the Tamil community, but his efforts in this regard proved to be in vain.

facts.text: The Congress was defeated in the 1989 general elections; the Janata Dal coalition formed and Vishwanath Pratap Singh became Prime Minister; his most important contribution was the OBC reservation policy.
facts.quote: The Congress party was defeated in the general elections held in 1989. Several political parties formed a coalition called the Janata Dal and Vishwanath Pratap Singh became the next Prime Minister of India. The policy for providing reservations for other backward classes (OBC) is considered to be his most important contribution.

facts.text: In 1990 Chandra Shekhar became Prime Minister; his government was also short-lived.
facts.quote: In 1990, Chandra Shekhar became the Prime Minister of India. His government was also short-lived.

facts.text: In 1991, during the election campaign, the LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelum) of Sri Lanka assassinated Rajiv Gandhi.
facts.quote: In 1991, during the election campaign, the terrorist organisation in Sri Lanka, Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelum (LTTE), assassinated Rajiv Gandhi.

facts.text: Towards the end of the 1980s unrest in Jammu and Kashmir began; terrorist activities forced the Kashmiri Pandits to leave the valley.
facts.quote: Towards the end of the decade of 1980s, the unrest in Jammu and Kashmir had begun. ... The terrorist activities there forced the Kashmiri Pandits to leave the valley.

facts.text: In 1991 the Soviet Russia disintegrated into several small countries and the Cold War came to an end; in India the government of P.V. Narasimha Rao initiated many economic changes.
facts.quote: The year 1991 is held to be very important in the history of the world as well as India. The Soviet Russia disintegrated into several different small countries and the Cold War came to an end. In India, the Government under the leadership of Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao initiated many changes in the Indian economy.

facts.text: In the elections between 1996 and 1999 no party got a clear majority in the Lok Sabha; Atal Bihari Vajpayee, H.D. Devegowda and Inder Kumar Gujral worked as Prime Ministers.
facts.quote: In the elections conducted between 1996 and 1999, no political party got a clear majority in the Lok Sabha. Atal Bihari Vajpayee, H.D. Devegowda and Inder Kumar Gujral worked as Prime Ministers in this period amongst them.

facts.text: In 1999 the 'National Democratic Alliance' came to power under the flag of Bharatiya Janata Party and Atal Bihari Vajpayee became Prime Minister.
facts.quote: Finally, in 1999 the 'National Democratic Alliance' came to power under the flag of Bharatiya Janata Party and Atal Bihari Vajpayee became India's Prime Minister.

facts.text: Atal Bihari Vajpayee tried to establish a dialogue with Pakistan but was not successful.
facts.quote: Atal Bihari Vajpayee tried to establish a dialogue with Pakistan but was not successful.

facts.text: India conducted a number of nuclear tests in 1998 and declared herself an atomic power.
facts.quote: India conducted a number of nuclear tests in 1998 and declared herself as an atomic power.

facts.text: In 1999 there was war between India and Pakistan in the Kargil region over the Kashmir issue; India defeated Pakistan.
facts.quote: In 1999, there was war between India and Pakistan in Kargil region over the Kashmir issue. India defeated Pakistan in this war.

facts.text: Modernisation, economic self-sufficiency and social justice have been characteristics of the Indian economy; the National Planning Commission coordinated development through Five Year Plans.
facts.quote: Right from independence, the modernisation of economy, economic self-sufficiency and social justice have been the characteristics of Indian economy. ... the National Planning Commission was established that would coordinate development through the policy of Five Year Plans.

facts.text: The Narasimha Rao Government started economic reforms from 1991, called economic liberalisation; foreign investment increased and information technology opened jobs; the changes are also called 'globalisation'.
facts.quote: The Narasimha Rao Government started economic reforms from 1991. These economic reforms are called as economic liberalisation. ... The foreign investment in India increased. ... The changes after 1991 are also described as 'globalisation'.

facts.text: Dr M. S. Swaminathan is known as the father of the Green Revolution in 1965; he increased foodgrain production with new scientific techniques.
facts.quote: Dr M. S. Swaminathan is known as the father of the Green Revolution in 1965. He implemented new scientific agricultural techniques and increased the production of foodgrains.

facts.text: The co-operative dairy experiment of Dr. Verghese Kurien increased milk production in India; this is called the 'White Revolution'.
facts.quote: The experiment in co-operative dairy movement by Dr. Verghese Kurien led to increase of milk production in India. This is called as 'White Revolution'.

facts.text: Dr. Homi Bhabha laid the foundation of the Indian atomic power programme; India insisted on peaceful uses like electricity, pharmaceuticals and defence.
facts.quote: Dr. Homi Bhabha laid the foundation of the Indian atomic power programme. India insisted on using atomic energy for peaceful purposes like generation of electricity, pharmaceuticals and defence.

facts.text: In 1975 India's first satellite 'Aryabhatta' was launched.
facts.quote: In 1975, the first satellite 'Aryabhatta' was launched.

facts.text: A separate 'Department of Women and Child Development' was created in 1985 under the Ministry of Human Resource Development.
facts.quote: a separate 'Department of Women and Child Development' was created in 1985 under the Ministry of Human Resource Development.

facts.text: Laws for social justice to women include the Prohibition of Dowry Act and the Equal Remuneration Act; the 73rd and 74th Constitution Amendments reserved seats for women in local self-government bodies.
facts.quote: They include the Prohibition of Dowry Act, Equal Remuneration Act. As per the 73rd and 74th Constitution Amendments, seats were reserved for women in the local self-government bodies.

facts.text: The 'Kakasaheb Kalelkar Commission' was set up in 1953 to recommend ways to improve the condition of those deprived due to the caste system.
facts.quote: The 'Kakasaheb Kalelkar Commission' was set up in 1953 to make recommendations so as to improve their condition.

facts.text: In 1978 a commission was constituted under the chairmanship of B. P. Mandal to study the issue of the other backward classes.
facts.quote: In 1978, a commission was constituted under the chairmanship of B. P. Mandal to study the issue of the other backward classes.

facts.text: The Government passed the Prevention of Atrocities Act in 1989 so that Scheduled castes and tribes could live with dignity and respect, free from fear and violence.
facts.quote: The Government passed the Prevention of Atrocities Act in 1989 to enable those belonging to the Scheduled castes and tribes to live with dignity and respect, free from fear, violence and oppression of the upper classes.

facts.text: Globalisation brought a revolution in telecommunication: mobile phones, internet and satellite communication spread across the country, changing the lifestyle, dietary habits, clothing, language and beliefs of the youth.
facts.quote: India has experienced an important revolution in the field of telecommunication technology. Mobile phones, internet and the communication facilities based on satellite have spread all across the country. ... These changes are visible from their dietary habits, clothing, language and beliefs.
